metadata.title: SpaceX’s Texas Terafab Could Become World’s Largest Building

content.text:
This story was originally published on CRE Daily. Join 70,000+ commercial real estate professionals getting daily news, market insights, and industry analysis delivered straight to their inbox with the free CRE Daily newsletter.
Key Takeaways
-
SpaceX and Tesla are planning a massive Terafab semiconductor facility in Grimes County, Texas, designed to produce AI chips for future technologies.
-
The proposed campus could span 100 million square feet across four phases, attract $119 billion in investment, and create roughly 3,000 jobs.
-
The project highlights Texas' growing appeal for advanced manufacturing campuses that combine major capital investment with long-term employment growth.
SpaceX and Tesla are planning what could become the world's largest building: a 100 million-square-foot semiconductor manufacturing campus in rural Grimes County, Texas, as described by CoStar. The proposed Terafab facility would support SpaceX's space-based data center ambitions while supplying chips for Tesla's Optimus robots and autonomous Cybercabs.
Located about 75 miles northwest of Houston and roughly 30 miles east of Texas A&M University, the project would transform a county of about 30,000 residents into the center of one of the largest industrial developments ever proposed.
Texas semiconductor manufacturing bet
SpaceX's Terafab represents a major expansion of Elon Musk's Texas manufacturing footprint. The company relocated its headquarters to Starbase, Texas, in 2024 and already operates major facilities in Bastrop and McGregor.
Tesla has also expanded aggressively in the state, moving its headquarters to Austin in 2021 and continuing to grow its Gigafactory campus, which is expected to exceed 15 million square feet by the end of 2026.
The Terafab project would take that industrial strategy to a different scale by combining chip production, advanced packaging, and related manufacturing operations under one roof.
The details
SpaceX's planned semiconductor facility would be built in four phases, with a total projected investment of $119 billion, according to the company's state incentive application. The campus could span 100 million square feet, making it roughly the size of 15 U.S. Pentagons.
The facility would produce advanced chips capable of supporting 1 terawatt of computing capacity annually. SpaceX plans to use the chips for future space-based data centers, while Tesla would deploy them across AI-driven applications, including Optimus humanoid robots and autonomous Cybercabs.
Texas Gov. Greg Abbott said the project qualifies for up to $30 million from the Texas Enterprise Fund, a state program aimed at attracting major employers. SpaceX expects the development to create approximately 3,000 jobs.
